key_insight: Generative approaches (e.g., diffusion models) that optimize hypervolume can still fail on other MOO metrics because of an "offline-frontier shift": the learned distribution shifts away from the true Pareto front represented in the offline dataset, reducing accuracy and coverage.
problem_solved: Diagnoses why state-of-the-art generative methods for offline multi-objective optimization underperform on established metrics (like generational distance and coverage) despite strong hypervolume scores, exposing a distributional limit tied to static training data.
method: Systematic empirical comparison of generative models (including diffusion-based) against evolutionary baselines across multiple MOO metrics and benchmarks.
Characterization and quantification of the "offline-frontier shift"—the distributional gap between dataset frontier and true Pareto front—via targeted diagnostics and metric analyses.
Provide practical evaluation guidelines and diagnostic tests to reveal when generative MOO models produce misleadingly high hypervolume but poor Pareto accuracy/diversity.
impact: Alerts practitioners to the danger of relying on hypervolume alone when evaluating generative MOO methods, and provides diagnostics and guidance to choose or design models and datasets that better recover true Pareto solutions.
visual_elements: Schematic diagram of the offline-frontier shift: dataset frontier vs true Pareto front with arrows showing learned distribution drift.
Side-by-side bar chart comparing methods on hypervolume vs generational distance vs coverage to highlight metric-specific trade-offs.
Pareto scatter plots showing example outputs from a generative model and an evolutionary baseline to visualize gaps in accuracy and diversity.
Flowchart of the recommended diagnostic pipeline (metrics to compute, decision thresholds, and follow-up steps).
paper_title: The Offline-Frontier Shift: Diagnosing Distributional Limits in Generative Multi-Objective Optimization
paper_authors: Stephanie Holly, Alexandru-Ciprian Zăvoianu, Siegfried Silber, Sepp Hochreiter, Werner Zellinger
